title: 13 Years of Brutal Business Truths: Priorities, Talent, Brand and Getting Better
summary: Alex Hormozi compresses 13 years of business lessons into eleven truths. Core themes: sell premium before selling to the masses, solve the real constraint, hire A-level talent, get better rather than bigger, protect deep-work time, and build brand through consistent delivery.

principles.text: Sell premium to rich people first; the middle and mass market require huge infrastructure and efficiency.
principles.quote: Sell to rich people until you have the money to sell all the poor people. The middle is where you get killed.

principles.text: Most founders lack priorities, not information. Define current state, desired state and obstacle before working.
principles.quote: if you can't clearly state current state, desired state, obstacle, you're running around like a chicken with your head cut off.

principles.text: Hiring A-level talent at higher pay is one of the biggest arbitrages in business; output multiple dwarfs cost.
principles.quote: I still think to this day one of the biggest arbitrage that exist in business is paying A talent A wages to get 10X the output.

principles.text: Better leads to growth, bigger leads to bloat. Growth is a lagging indicator of getting better.
principles.quote: Fundamentally, growth is a lagging indicator. The things you do to create growth are the leading indicators.

principles.text: Protect the first hours of your day for the highest-leverage work and let non-existential fires burn.
principles.quote: I work uninterrupted for the first four to six hours of my day on the things that I think have the highest leverage in the business.

principles.text: Break your money-making system into its smallest input actions and ask why you can't 10x them to find the constraint.
principles.quote: you can quickly understand where the constraint of the business is by simply asking why can't we 10x this?
